PROBLEM: Agent runtimes emit ad hoc span names, so cross-system comparison, sampling, and cost attribution are impossible.
MECHANISM: Named operations: invoke_agent, invoke_workflow, plan, execute_tool, retrieval, search_memory, plus memory create/update/upsert/delete. Agent attributes gen_ai.agent.id/name/version/description. Requested vs response model, provider, output type, finish reasons. Token usage with cache read/write subsets and billed-vs-consumed distinction. Duration, time-to-first-chunk/token, time-per-output-token metrics. Evaluation event gen_ai.evaluation.result. All conventions carry Development status, not Stable.
INVARIANT: Sampling-relevant attributes (provider, operation, agent name, requested model, server address/port) are available at span creation when used for sampling decisions.
FAILURE_MODEL: Development status means attribute names may change; consumers must not treat them as stable. Content attributes (inputs, outputs, system instructions, tool definitions) are opt-in and may be filtered or truncated by instrumentations.
SECURITY_MODEL: Content attributes are explicitly sensitive and opt-in; the spec expects filtering/truncation but defines no redaction mechanism.
SCALING_MODEL: Attribute cardinality stays bounded by keeping content opt-in; usage and duration metrics are pre-aggregatable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX adopts the taxonomy as the canonical span and event vocabulary for ping_events: invoke_agent for mission execution, execute_tool for canonical worker tool steps, memory operations for knowledge and memory events. CRX adds authorization receipts, causation lineage, and canonical authorities, which the taxonomy does not define.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: The taxonomy is an observation vocabulary for transport; CRX semantics (authorization, causation, canonical truth) are separate layers the taxonomy cannot express.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: vocabulary mapping document plus attribute name alignment in projections.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: interoperability with OTLP backends and no custom taxonomy to maintain.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Export a CRX mission trace as OTLP; any CRX semantic the taxonomy cannot express (auth receipt, causation) must appear as a documented CRX extension attribute, never shoehorned into an unrelated OTel attribute.

PROBLEM: Tool calls cross process boundaries over MCP JSON-RPC, where ambient trace context does not survive.
MECHANISM: W3C traceparent, tracestate, and baggage are propagated inside MCP JSON-RPC params._meta. The MCP server span uses the extracted context as its remote parent. The ambient transport context is recorded as a span link, because MCP and HTTP transport contexts are independent.
INVARIANT: Every MCP server span has either a remote parent taken from _meta or an explicit link recording the ambient transport context; no span claims a parent it did not receive.
FAILURE_MODEL: A proxy that strips _meta silently breaks lineage; the link records the break instead of hiding it.
SECURITY_MODEL: params._meta is client-writable; inbound parent claims are untrusted hints until the receiving authority validates the mission or causation ID against its own journal.
SCALING_MODEL: Constant per-call header cost.
CRX_ANALOG: Canonical workers reify results as canonical events and disposable subagents return results automatically; CRX uses _meta-style propagation for causation IDs across the worker boundary, with ingress validating every claimed parent against ping_events before attaching lineage.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: OTel propagation carries observation context only and accepts it; CRX carries authorization plus causation and must verify, not just accept.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: canonicalization of inbound parent claims at fail-closed ingress.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: missing-parent and orphan-task detection across worker boundaries.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Send a tool request carrying a forged _meta parent; CRX ingress must reject or quarantine it, never attach the execution to the forged lineage.

PROBLEM: Systems synthesize conversation IDs from UUIDs, trace IDs, or content hashes, creating false continuity between unrelated runs.
MECHANISM: Spec rule: use a genuine available conversation ID; do not synthesize one from a UUID, trace ID, or content hash as a fallback.
INVARIANT: A conversation ID present on a span is either the provider's genuine ID or absent; absence is explicit.
FAILURE_MODEL: When no genuine ID exists, the attribute is omitted, never fabricated.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Not applicable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX mission IDs are idempotent and deterministic; the same discipline applies: never fabricate a mission or correlation ID to fill a gap, record absence explicitly as a typed state.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX goes further with deterministic IDs; the shared principle is no fabrication.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: validation rule at event canonicalization.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: prevents false lineage merges that would corrupt replay.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Attempt to emit an event with a synthesized conversation ID; canonicalization must reject it or mark it explicitly synthetic.

PROBLEM: Transient in-memory agent IDs get treated as stable identity across restarts.
MECHANISM: Agent attributes gen_ai.agent.id, name, version, description, with a spec warning against using transient in-memory IDs as stable agent IDs.
INVARIANT: An agent ID that persists across restarts refers to the same agent definition.
FAILURE_MODEL: Process restart invalidates transient IDs; consumers must not join telemetry on them.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Not applicable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX has one authority per identity; agent identity is issued by the identity authority, never generated ad hoc by workers.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: OTel warns; CRX enforces through the identity authority.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: identity issuance rule.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: prevents cross-run identity confusion in replay.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Restart a worker; assert no new agent identity is minted for the same logical agent.

PROBLEM: Agent runs need structure beyond LLM spans: task scope, turns, handoffs between agents, guardrail checks, MCP discovery.
MECHANISM: Span types: task (top-level Runner run), turn (turn number, agent name, usage), agent (name, available handoffs, tools, output type), handoff (source and destination agents), guardrail (name, triggered), MCP list tools, function/tool, generation, response, custom. Parent defaults from trace/span context but can be supplied explicitly.
INVARIANT: Every span resolves a parent from context or from an explicit override; a turn span records its turn number.
FAILURE_MODEL: Trace creation warns when a trace already exists but creates another anyway (see OBS-OAIAG-DEDUP-WARN); IDs are random UUID-derived, not deterministic.
SECURITY_MODEL: None beyond export-time sanitization (see OBS-OAIAG-EXPORT-SANITIZE).
SCALING_MODEL: Per-span overhead; turn spans make loop iterations observably bounded.
CRX_ANALOG: Mission execution maps to task spans, worker turns to turn spans, delegation between subagents to handoff spans with source and destination, constitutional guardrail evaluations to guardrail spans with a triggered flag.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX handoffs carry authorization receipts; OTel handoffs record only that a handoff occurred. CRX IDs are deterministic; the SDK mints random UUIDs.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: map CRX event types to span kinds and emit from canonical workers.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: a standard agent-run shape consumable by any OTLP tool.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Run a multi-turn mission with a handoff; assert the exported trace contains task, turn, agent, and handoff spans with correct parentage.

PROBLEM: Duplicate trace creation corrupts lineage.
MECHANISM: trace() warns if a trace already exists in context but creates another trace anyway; detection without prevention.
INVARIANT: None enforceable; the warning is advisory.
FAILURE_MODEL: Warn-and-continue leaves two live traces and downstream consumers cannot tell which is canonical.
SECURITY_MODEL: None.
SCALING_MODEL: Not applicable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX missions use idempotent deterministic IDs; warn-only dedup would violate the deterministic-ID guarantee and the fail-closed ingress rule.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX must fail closed or return the existing trace; detection without prevention is insufficient for a canonical journal.
INTEGRATION_COST: Not applicable.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Negative lesson: documents why CRX needs fail-closed ingress dedup on deterministic IDs.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Not applicable; rejected mechanism.

PROBLEM: Reasoning content and sensitive payloads leak to the tracing backend.
MECHANISM: BackendSpanExporter sanitizes payloads for the OpenAI tracing API (_should_sanitize_for_openai_tracing_api, _sanitize_for_openai_tracing_api) and strips generation reasoning items before export (_omit_generation_reasoning).
INVARIANT: Items sent to the OpenAI tracing API never contain generation reasoning content.
FAILURE_MODEL: Sanitization is exporter-specific; any other exporter receives unsanitized payloads (same re-leak class as Langfuse two-stage masking).
SECURITY_MODEL: Defense in depth: sanitize at export, not only at capture.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-export traversal cost over payload items.
CRX_ANALOG: The CRX observation authority applies export-stage redaction before any external sink; the canonical journal retains full evidence internally and redaction is per-sink.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX separates canonical evidence (full) from observations (redacted); the SDK conflates span storage with export.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: redaction hook at the observation export boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: prevents reasoning-trace leakage to third-party backends.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Attach a second exporter; assert it does not receive reasoning content unless explicitly authorized, documenting the re-leak boundary that the observation authority must close.

PROBLEM: Duplicate execution starts need detection.
MECHANISM: _started_trace_ids: a bounded in-process 4096-entry ordered set of started trace IDs.
INVARIANT: None durable; entries evict after 4096 and the set dies with the process.
FAILURE_MODEL: Process restart wipes the set; multi-worker deployments hold disjoint sets; eviction re-admits duplicates silently.
SECURITY_MODEL: None.
SCALING_MODEL: Bounded memory, at the cost of correctness.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX duplicate-execution detection must be journal-backed: a unique constraint on the deterministic execution key in ping_events, visible to every worker.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX needs durability and cross-worker visibility; the SDK set provides neither.
INTEGRATION_COST: Not applicable.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Negative lesson: in-memory dedup sets are not duplicate-execution protection.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Not applicable; rejected mechanism.

LICENSE: Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2): source-available, not OSI-approved; pattern-only, do not vendor code
PROBLEM: Agent traces need domain span kinds plus evaluations that are queryable apart from spans.
MECHANISM: Span kinds TOOL, CHAIN, LLM, PROMPT, RETRIEVER, EMBEDDING, AGENT, RERANKER, EVALUATOR, GUARDRAIL, UNKNOWN. SpanContext carries trace and span IDs with a nullable parent_id (null means root). Typed events including exceptions. Conversation ID extension. Span evaluations are separately keyed records linked to their subject spans, not span attributes.
INVARIANT: Null parent_id if and only if root span; every evaluation references its subject span, never floats unattached.
FAILURE_MODEL: UNKNOWN is a typed admission of ignorance rather than a silent default; evaluations keyed to missing spans are detectable.
SECURITY_MODEL: No authorization model; topology is trusted as reported.
SCALING_MODEL: Evaluations as separate keyed records keep span payloads small and evaluable independently.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX span vocabulary for mission traces; evaluations become canonical evaluation events linked by causation ID; GUARDRAIL spans map to constitutional-concern evaluations; null parent maps to mission-root detection.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: Phoenix evaluates after the fact; CRX guardrail evaluations can gate execution fail-closed before effects happen.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: span-kind mapping plus an evaluation event type in the journal.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: trace topology plus typed evaluation linkage without dashboard-only thinking.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Emit an evaluation naming a nonexistent span; the store must reject it rather than storing a dangling evaluation.

PROBLEM: Inconsistent attribute names for inputs, outputs, tokens, tools, retrieval, and sessions across instrumentations.
MECHANISM: Standardized attributes: input.value, output.value, llm.token_count.*, tool parameters, retrieval documents, metadata, session.id, user.id, evaluation name and metadata.
INVARIANT: The same semantic always uses the same attribute key across instrumentations.
FAILURE_MODEL: Missing attributes are absent, not zero-filled; no source-level redaction or sampling mechanism was found, so absence of redaction must not be mistaken for a redaction guarantee.
SECURITY_MODEL: None defined at this layer.
SCALING_MODEL: Flat string-keyed attributes; low overhead.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX canonical event attribute vocabulary for ping_events projections; session.id maps to mission scope, user.id to the identity authority.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: OTel attributes are conventions; CRX attributes are canonical and typed by the journal schema.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: adopt the key names in projection schemas.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: one attribute vocabulary shared with the OTel ecosystem.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Project two different CRX events carrying the same semantic; assert identical attribute keys in both projections.

PROBLEM: Sensitive data enters telemetry through SDK APIs and through third-party OpenTelemetry instrumentation the SDK does not control.
MECHANISM: Two independent masking hooks: SDK-level mask() for data set through Langfuse APIs, and export-stage mask_otel_spans() applied to final OTel span attributes, which also covers third-party instrumentation.
INVARIANT: Export-stage masking covers spans regardless of which instrumentation created them.
FAILURE_MODEL: Export-stage masking does not alter spans already exported through other exporters; masking is per-pipeline, so a second exporter re-leaks raw values.
SECURITY_MODEL: Mask functions run on the client; the backend only avoids seeing raw values if no unmasked exporter exists.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-span hook cost at export time.
CRX_ANALOG: The CRX observation authority applies capture-time classification plus export-stage redaction per sink, and documents the multi-sink re-leak boundary explicitly; all sinks route through the authority.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX can enforce single-authority sink routing; Langfuse cannot, because exporters are user-composed.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: redaction hooks at capture and at each export boundary.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: prevents third-party instrumentation from bypassing SDK-level masking.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Configure two exporters with masking on one; assert the unmasked exporter still receives raw values, proving the boundary, then route every sink through the observation authority and re-assert.

PROBLEM: Trace-level attributes such as tenant and environment must reach every child span.
MECHANISM: Trace-level attributes are propagated to child spans through context and baggage.
INVARIANT: A child span carries the trace-level attributes of its trace.
FAILURE_MODEL: Baggage size limits can truncate propagation on deep traces.
SECURITY_MODEL: Baggage is in-band and mutable by intermediaries; treat propagated attributes as hints, not authority.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-span attribute copy cost, bounded by baggage limits.
CRX_ANALOG: Mission-level attributes (mission ID, policy version, tenant) propagate to all derived events through causation context, and the journal records what was propagated.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX propagation is journal-recorded and therefore auditable; baggage propagation is in-band only.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: propagation rule in the causation context.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: consistent mission scoping across derived events.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Start a trace with a tenant attribute; assert a deeply nested child span carries it, and assert the journal records the propagation.

PROBLEM: Evidence and artifacts need stable, content-addressed references that survive renames and moves.
MECHANISM: Durable typed references: object and op references embed a digest; call references address call IDs; explicit agent-turn, agent-conversation, and agent-span references; weave:/// URI scheme. TableRef.digest raises WeaveDigestError when the digest is not a string, a typed failure instead of a silent default.
INVARIANT: A reference without a valid digest is rejected at construction; a digest binds the reference to content.
FAILURE_MODEL: Digest mismatch means the referenced object changed; refs do not silently follow the new content.
SECURITY_MODEL: Digest binding makes tampering detectable at resolution time.
SCALING_MODEL: Refs are small strings; resolution is lazy.
CRX_ANALOG: The CRX evidence authority issues content-addressed evidence refs via the hash authority; witness receipts address canonical events by ID plus hash; every mutation cites its receipt ref.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX refs are canonical and single-authority; Weave refs are client-constructed and backend-resolved.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: evidence ref format, digest computation, and resolution path.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: directly enables the mutation-without-receipt check (every mutation cites a verifiable receipt ref).
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Construct a ref with a tampered digest; resolution must fail closed, never resolve to the tampered object.

PROBLEM: Feedback must attach to the exact artifact evaluated, not to a nearby span by convention.
MECHANISM: Typed feedback records addressed to object and call references; the call model carries trace_id, parent_id, call ID, thread ID, and turn ID.
INVARIANT: Every feedback record names its subject ref; unaddressed feedback is not representable.
FAILURE_MODEL: Feedback against a deleted or unknown ref is detectable at write time.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Feedback is write-light and indexed by subject ref.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX evaluation events linked by causation ID to the exact evaluated execution; feedback becomes journal evidence rather than dashboard decoration.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX feedback is a canonical event with hash and witness; Weave feedback is a backend record.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low to medium: evaluation event type with subject addressing.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: precise evaluation linkage for autonomous throughput measurement.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Write feedback against a nonexistent ref; the journal must reject it.

PROBLEM: Manual span creation is verbose and inconsistent across an agent codebase.
MECHANISM: Decorators for workflow, task, agent, tool, guardrail, conversation, plus async variants. Agent delegates to workflow semantics; tool delegates to task semantics. Attributes include traceloop.span.kind, entity name/path/version, entity input/output, association properties, and prompt key/version/hash/template/template variables.
INVARIANT: A decorated function always emits a span, including on exception, with the exception recorded.
FAILURE_MODEL: Undecorated helper calls are invisible; decorator coverage is a code-review concern, not an enforced property.
SECURITY_MODEL: None; decorators observe, they do not authorize.
SCALING_MODEL: Negligible per-call overhead beyond the span itself.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX canonical workers use instrumentation helpers that emit canonical events carrying entity version and prompt hash; mission-as-workflow delegation mirrors agent-delegates-to-workflow.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: Decorators emit observations; CRX workers emit canonical journal events with authority.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: worker instrumentation helpers in the canonical worker SDK.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: consistent instrumentation with low developer friction.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Decorate a function that raises; assert the span records the exception and still closes, and that the journal received the canonical event.

PROBLEM: Long-running agent sessions need observable state metadata for debugging stale or stuck runs.
MECHANISM: Span kinds include workflow, session, task, operation, agent, tool, llm, chain, guardrail. Attributes include total tool and LLM cost (gen_ai.usage.total_cost), workflow session id/name, session workflow/user IDs, state keys, state size, storage type, and created/updated timestamps.
INVARIANT: None enforced in source; the attributes are advisory only.
FAILURE_MODEL: Nothing checks staleness, enforces leases, or prevents commits against old snapshots; a stale session looks identical to a fresh one except for its timestamps.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Attribute-only; no enforcement cost.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX stale-snapshot execution detection needs exactly these signals (snapshot version, timestamps, state identity) but as commit preconditions enforced by the journal, not as advisory attributes.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: AgentOps describes state; CRX must gate on it.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: adopt the attribute vocabulary for snapshot metadata.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: vocabulary for the stale-snapshot check, with enforcement added by CRX.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Present a session whose updated timestamp predates the required snapshot version; assert CRX refuses to commit against it while the raw attributes alone would have allowed it.

PROBLEM: Trace context must cross SDK and backend boundaries and serialize compactly.
MECHANISM: W3C traceparent injection; Braintrust parent metadata carried in W3C baggage; exported parent strings allow adding spans to an existing trace; versioned span-identifier serialization where v4 compresses 32-hex trace IDs to 16 bytes and 16-hex span IDs to 8 bytes.
INVARIANT: Identifier serialization is versioned; the v4 parser rejects malformed input instead of guessing.
FAILURE_MODEL: Version mismatch across SDK and backend yields unparseable identifiers, which fail loudly rather than misattaching.
SECURITY_MODEL: Baggage-carried parent metadata is intermediary-mutable; validate before trusting.
SCALING_MODEL: Compact binary encoding halves identifier bytes on the wire.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX causation and correlation propagation across worker boundaries; compact canonical ID encoding for journal references.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: This is a propagation format only; CRX identity authority still mints every ID.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: adopt the versioned serialization discipline for propagated IDs.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: compact, versioned lineage propagation.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Round-trip a parent identifier through v4 serialization; assert byte-exact recovery, and feed malformed bytes to assert loud rejection.

LICENSE: GNU AGPL-3.0 (copyleft; do not vendor code into CRX)
PROBLEM: PII in telemetry needs detection before export.
MECHANISM: Regex-based PII detector covering phone, email, SSN, date of birth, credit card, and IP patterns; cost tables hard-coded per 1,000 tokens; trace utilities aggregate token counts and cost.
INVARIANT: None; the detector returns an empty list on any exception, converting detector failure into a finding of no PII.
FAILURE_MODEL: Any exception inside the detector silently becomes no findings, so PII passes through undetected; this is the exact failure-becomes-empty-success anti-pattern. Hard-coded cost tables go stale as provider pricing changes.
SECURITY_MODEL: Regexes are heuristic, not authoritative; combined with silent failure they provide false assurance.
SCALING_MODEL: Not applicable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX typed failures must never become empty success; a redaction failure must surface as a typed error that halts export, never as a clean bill of health.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: Not applicable; rejected as a mechanism, kept as a negative lesson.
INTEGRATION_COST: Not applicable.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Negative lesson with a concrete code specimen of the anti-pattern CRX forbids.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Not applicable; rejected mechanism.

SOURCE_PROJECT: LangSmith (docs only; repository not cloned, no source inspection)
PROBLEM: Tool results must be matched to the requests that caused them, especially under concurrency.
MECHANISM: Documentation recommends pairing tool results to requests by exact tool_call_id, falling back to tool name matching only when IDs are unavailable.
INVARIANT: Exact ID match is preferred; name fallback is explicitly documented as weaker.
FAILURE_MODEL: Name-only matching conflates concurrent identical tool calls; silent misattribution follows.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: ID join is index-friendly; name fallback is not.
CRX_ANALOG: The CRX tool-result-without-request check: an exact call-ID anti-join in ping_events between result events and request events within the same mission and trace.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: LangSmith documents the pairing as guidance; CRX enforces it as a journal invariant.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: indexed anti-join query over canonical events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: the cheapest reliable form of the tool-result-without-request check.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Run two concurrent identical tool calls; assert name-based pairing is ambiguous while ID-based pairing resolves exactly, and assert a result with no matching request ID is flagged.

SOURCE_PROJECT: LangSmith (docs only; repository not cloned, no source inspection)
PROBLEM: Run hierarchy and ordering need an explicit, queryable shape.
MECHANISM: Run shape carries run ID, trace ID, parent run ID, ancestor IDs, child IDs, run type (llm, chain, tool, retriever), status, inputs, outputs, error, events, tokens, cost, first-token time, feedback, attachments, and dotted_order for total ordering within a trace.
INVARIANT: dotted_order gives a total order of runs within a trace.
FAILURE_MODEL: Client-reported parentage is trusted as reported; no independent verification is documented.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Denormalized ancestor and child ID lists trade write cost for read speed.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX mission and step hierarchy with causation IDs and journal sequence ordering; dotted_order maps to the journal sequence as the canonical order.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX parentage is validated at ingress against the journal; LangSmith accepts client-reported parentage.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: hierarchy fields on canonical events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: a proven run-shape vocabulary for hierarchy queries.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Submit a run naming a nonexistent parent; CRX ingress must reject it where the documented shape alone would accept it.

PROBLEM: Requests need grouping into sessions with hierarchy without requiring a full span tree.
MECHANISM: Helicone-Session-Id, Helicone-Session-Path, and Helicone-Session-Name headers parsed from the request in shared/proxy/heliconeHeaders.ts; parentage is encoded as a hierarchical path string such as /abstract/outline/lesson-1.
INVARIANT: A session path's parent is its string prefix; the path encodes the hierarchy.
FAILURE_MODEL: Path-string parentage is fragile: renaming a mid-path segment breaks lineage, there is no referential integrity, and distinct sessions can collide on path strings.
SECURITY_MODEL: Headers are client-supplied; session membership is asserted, not authorized.
SCALING_MODEL: Zero storage cost beyond the header values.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX adopts header-style session tagging for mission grouping but keeps explicit parent IDs for lineage; the path-prefix orphan check becomes an ID-existence check against ping_events.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: Helicone parentage is conventional and string-based; CRX parentage is referential and validated.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: session tag headers plus parent-ID validation.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: cheap session grouping with real orphan detection.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Rename a mid-path segment; assert Helicone-style lineage breaks while CRX ID-based lineage survives, and assert a session naming a nonexistent parent is flagged as orphan.

PROBLEM: Floating-point cost accumulation loses cents at scale.
MECHANISM: COST_PRECISION_MULTIPLIER = 1_000_000_000; costs stored as integers in ClickHouse; cost derived from the response usage block and the response model through per-provider pricing tables in packages/cost.
INVARIANT: Stored cost times 1e-9 equals USD; every cost figure is traceable to a usage block plus a model price.
FAILURE_MODEL: Pricing tables must track provider changes; streaming requests need stream-usage flags or token counts (and therefore costs) are wrong.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Integer arithmetic; pricing tables are loaded once.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX cost attribution per mission and step stored in integer minor units; cost figures cite their pricing source.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX pricing versions come from the config authority so stale prices are detectable (see OBS-OPIK-COST-VERSION).
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: integer minor-unit cost storage.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: exact cost accounting for autonomous throughput economics.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Sum one million micro-costs in float versus integer; assert the float drifts and the integer does not.

PROBLEM: Some requests must not have their bodies persisted at all.
MECHANISM: omitRequestLog and omitResponseLog booleans on the handler context; the request and response body handlers skip persisting bodies when the flags are set.
INVARIANT: When omit flags are set, no body bytes reach the store.
FAILURE_MODEL: Omission is body-scoped, not record-scoped: metadata such as timestamps, model, and cost may still be recorded.
SECURITY_MODEL: Reduces blast radius for sensitive payloads; the flags themselves must be set by policy, not by the untrusted caller alone.
SCALING_MODEL: Saves storage and keeps hot paths fast.
CRX_ANALOG: The CRX observation authority applies per-mission redaction policy; the canonical journal keeps hashes for proof even when bodies are omitted.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX keeps a receipt (hash) even when the body is omitted; Helicone drops the body without a content receipt.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: redaction flags on the observation export path.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: principled body omission with proof of omission.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Set the omit flags; assert the store contains no body bytes while the request record and its hash receipt still exist.

PROBLEM: Provider pricing changes silently invalidate historical cost figures.
MECHANISM: totalEstimatedCostVersion string stored alongside totalEstimatedCost; pricing-formula changes trigger recomputation of affected costs. Span usage is an open-vocabulary integer map whose keys (for example cached-token detail keys) are interpreted later by the cost calculator.
INVARIANT: Every cost figure names the pricing version that produced it.
FAILURE_MODEL: Unversioned costs silently go stale; open-vocabulary usage keys require the calculator to know every key.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Recomputation is batched on pricing changes.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX cost attribution carries the config-authority pricing version; the stale-cost check compares declared version against current policy.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX pricing versions are issued by the config authority, making staleness a first-class detectable state.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: version field on cost records plus a recomputation trigger.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: costs that stay truthful across pricing changes.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Change a model price; assert costs computed under the old version are flagged for recomputation rather than silently kept.

PROBLEM: Trace list views must not join spans on every read.
MECHANISM: A trace is shaped as a root span plus denormalized read-side aggregates: summed usage, totalEstimatedCost, spanCount, llmSpanCount, hasToolSpans, unique provider list, span feedback scores averaged by name onto the trace, guardrailsValidations, threadId, visibilityMode, experiment reference. INVARIANT: Aggregates are read-side caches recomputed from spans; they are never source truth.
FAILURE_MODEL: Aggregates drift if recomputation lags ingestion; readers must be able to rebuild from spans.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Denormalization trades write amplification for read speed.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX projections over ping_events: precomputed mission summaries owned by the projection authority with deterministic replay; the journal stays canonical.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX projections are authority-owned and replayable; Opik aggregates are backend-computed caches.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: projection schemas for mission summaries.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: fast mission list views without endangering journal truth.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Ingest spans after the aggregate snapshot; assert the projection rebuilds deterministically from the journal and matches.

PROBLEM: Telemetry ingestion must not block the application.
MECHANISM: Asynchronous fire-and-forget pipeline: API to Message to Streamer to Queue to Consumer to REST client to backend, with batching and automatic retries; the application must call flush() before exit or buffered telemetry is lost.
INVARIANT: None durable; unflushed telemetry is lost on crash.
FAILURE_MODEL: A crash before flush loses telemetry silently; the observability system itself becomes negatively observable: missing spans with no record of the loss.
SECURITY_MODEL: None specific.
SCALING_MODEL: Batching keeps overhead low at high span volume.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX canonical events are acknowledged journal writes; telemetry that can be silently lost is not evidence and cannot back replay or witness.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: CRX requires durable, acknowledged writes; fire-and-forget is the opposite trade.
INTEGRATION_COST: Not applicable.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Negative lesson: the 2026-09-22 CRX gap (telemetry classes exist but are unwired and tables are empty) must be closed with acknowledged journal writes, not best-effort exporters.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Not applicable; rejected mechanism.

SOURCE_PROJECT: AI45Lab/AgentDoG (research framework; paper COLM 2025, arxiv 2601.18491; repository not cloned)
SOURCE_COMMIT: n/a (paper and repository documentation level; not source-verified)
PROBLEM: Binary safe/unsafe labels cannot diagnose why an agent trajectory failed.
MECHANISM: Trajectory-level diagnostic guardrail with a three-dimensional taxonomy: Risk Source by Failure Mode by Risk Consequence. An Agentic XAI Attribution module traces unsafe actions back to specific trajectory steps and sentences using information-theoretic attribution scores. Failure modes include Unconfirmed or Over-privileged Action, Tool Misuse in Specific Context, Failure to Validate Tool Outputs, Unauthorized Information Disclosure, and Procedural Deviation or Inaction.
INVARIANT: None deterministic; judgments are model-produced and probabilistic.
FAILURE_MODEL: Judge-model errors produce misdiagnosis; the framework is diagnostic, not a gate, and must never block execution on its own.
SECURITY_MODEL: The judge sees full trajectories, so trajectory content must be handled as sensitive.
SCALING_MODEL: Per-trajectory model inference cost; suitable for sampled or post-incident analysis, not per-step gating.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX adopts the failure-mode vocabulary as evaluation labels on journal replays for post-incident diagnosis and probe design; the deterministic journal invariants remain the gate.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: AgentDoG diagnoses with models; CRX detects with journal queries. Complementary, not substitutable.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low for vocabulary adoption; high if the judge models are ever run (not recommended as a gate).
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: a shared diagnostic vocabulary for the exact failure classes CRX must detect deterministically.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Replay a known tool-misuse incident from the journal; assert the taxonomy labels it correctly and assert the deterministic journal check fires independently of the model judgment.

SOURCE_PROJECT: openguardrails/openguardrails (protocol proposal; README level, repository not cloned)
PROBLEM: Agent traffic needs a wire model in which requests and responses are pairable by construction.
MECHANISM: Layered model: L6 Session (one conversation), L5 Turn (one instruction to quiescence), L4 Step (one model call with request and response paired by step_id), L3 Event (one GuardEvent, half a step, the only layer on the wire), L2 Call (one tool call the model asked for), L1 Exec (one real execution on a machine).
INVARIANT: Every response pairs to exactly one request via step_id; an Event is always half of a Step, so unpaired halves are detectable by construction.
FAILURE_MODEL: A missing half is visible as an unpaired event rather than as silent absence.
SECURITY_MODEL: The contract names executions but does not authorize them; authorization stays out of band.
SCALING_MODEL: Constant per-event cost.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX tool request and result pairing via call IDs; step_id-style pairing informs the canonical event schema for model calls so halves are joinable in the journal.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: OGR is a protocol proposal; CRX implements the pairing as enforced journal invariants.
INTEGRATION_COST: Low: step and event pairing fields on canonical events.
EXPECTED_VALUE: High: makes tool-result-without-request and missing-half failures structurally detectable.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Emit a response event with no matching request half; the journal must surface it as an unpaired half.

SOURCE_PROJECT: redhatproductsecurity/ai-guardian (changelog and docs level; repository not cloned)
LICENSE: UNVERIFIED (Red Hat project; not locally verified)
PROBLEM: Agent traces locked in a vendor-specific format cannot reach standard backends.
MECHANISM: An otel export command converts agent traces (turns with step arrays, api_call and seq numbering, span IDs, enriched metadata) to OTLP JSON following the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions; hook session telemetry records adapter name, hook event counts, and token usage on root spans so even clean sessions produce observable traces.
INVARIANT: Exported spans carry GenAI semconv attribute names; session sequence numbering preserves hook invocation order.
FAILURE_MODEL: Export-time failures (trace too large, backend unreachable) must surface as typed export errors, never as silently partial exports; consumers must be able to distinguish no export from empty export.
SECURITY_MODEL: Exported traces may carry sensitive content; the export path needs the same redaction policy as any sink.
SCALING_MODEL: Export is offline and batchable.
CRX_ANALOG: CRX-to-OTLP bridge: project ping_events to GenAI semconv spans for external backends without making OTLP the canonical store; the journal stays canonical and the export is a projection.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: Export is a projection owned by the projection authority; it never replaces the journal.
INTEGRATION_COST: Medium: projection from journal events to GenAI semconv spans.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: CRX missions become visible in any OTLP backend with zero canonical compromise.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Export a mission trace; validate the OTLP JSON attribute names against the GenAI semconv spec and assert no canonical-only fields leak.

SOURCE_PROJECT: OpenObserve (v1.0 announcement 2026-09-22; product level, repository not cloned)
PROBLEM: Agent telemetry is stitched across separate tools for LLM sessions, traces, logs, and real-user monitoring, so a single request cannot be followed end to end.
MECHANISM: Version 1.0 unifies logs, metrics, traces, RUM, and AI observability in one Rust platform: token cost and usage tracking on by default across 80+ providers attributed per agent, full-session tracing of agent conversations including tool calls and database requests linked to session replay, an Agent Graph of agent interactions, and built-in evaluation (custom scorers, scheduled eval jobs, LLM-as-judge, annotation queues feeding the next eval round), plus a 1,200+ curated alert library.
INVARIANT: Cost tracking is on by default (opt-out, not opt-in).
FAILURE_MODEL: A unified platform is a larger blast radius and a self-hosting operations burden; evaluation features are only as good as their scorers.
SECURITY_MODEL: Single plane means a single compromise surface for all telemetry.
SCALING_MODEL: Rust core aimed at high-ingest throughput as a Datadog/Splunk/Elasticsearch alternative.
CRX_ANALOG: Thesis-level relevance only: CRX must not build a second orchestration universe, and a unified observation plane reduces stitching; CRX keeps ping_events canonical and projects into such a plane rather than replacing the journal with it.
SEMANTIC_DELTA: OpenObserve is an observation platform, not an agent runtime with authorization semantics; it cannot supply the journal invariants.
INTEGRATION_COST: Not applicable while watching.
EXPECTED_VALUE: Medium: convergence pressure to watch; if the platform matures, it becomes a candidate OTLP projection target.
FALSIFICATION_TEST: Not applicable; watch item.
